minutes.headline: Select Board granted a door-to-door peddler's license 4-1 and approved a coffee roaster license and a Boys and Girls Club tollbooth.
minutes.summary: The board heard a resident's update on saving the old primary school, then acted on a coffee roasting license, a peddler's license and a tollbooth request. It then heard a Complete Streets Tier three funding presentation for Main Street and the beach, with no decision recorded in the captions.

public_comment.topic: Reported on walking the old primary school with staff and meeting the town manager; opposes disposing of the building and plans a citizen petition for the fall ballot to fund the roof repair, needing 100 signatures in 13 days.

what_happened.line: The Select Board granted a door-to-door peddler's license to a financial advisor, 4-1, limited to 9:00 a.m. until sundown.
The board granted a common victualer license to a coffee roasting shop and cafe at 39 Mass Ave.
The board approved a Boys and Girls Club tollbooth for October 12, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., with volunteers 18 and over.
A resident urged keeping the old primary school and said a citizen petition would put the roof repair on the fall ballot, needing 100 signatures in 13 days.
The board heard a Complete Streets Tier three presentation for Main Street and the beach; the captions record no decision.

why_it_matters: The old primary school's fate may reach residents as a fall ballot question if the citizen petition gathers enough signatures.
Complete Streets funding could offset part of the cost of paving, drainage and ADA ramp and sidewalk work, which otherwise falls on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: Whether the citizen petition for the primary school roof repair collects its 100 signatures within the 13 days stated.
Whether the town applies for Complete Streets Tier three funding, and for which of the projects.
